properties.description: Answers the requirement's SHOWN WHEN clause by clause. (1) The everyday command builds and tests the workspace without librocksdb-sys compiling: `cargo dev-test` run whole, and `cargo tree --workspace --no-default-features -i librocksdb-sys` (no such package in the graph). (2) A release build still opens a store in a folder: the branch's release binary writes a design into a new folder and a second process reopens it and reads it back; and every test in the `on_disk` program runs on the default build. (3) A build without the feature refuses one with a message naming the fix: crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/a_build_without_on_disk_storage_refuses_a_store_in_a_folder.rs, written first and observed failing on main (4 of 4) — the library openers, the one-shot door (--export and a read of a real v0.76.0 store, --import and a write where none exists), a stdio server and a --shared client each refuse, name the build, the `rocksdb` feature and the fix, serve no design from memory, and leave the folder byte for byte as it was; with the feature, a real store opens. (4) The test names before and after match one to one with RocksDB, and without it lack exactly the listed disk tests: `cargo test -p reflow2-mcp -- --list` on main (e45225520) and on the branch, names normalised, compared in both configurations; and, standing, crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/every_test_file_runs_in_exactly_one_program.rs fails any test file declared in no program, in two, or a discovery switched back on. (5) The number of MCP test programs and the target directory's growth, measured before and after from `cargo clean -p reflow2-core -p reflow2-mcp`.
properties.findings: On branch feat/everyday-builds-run-without-rocksdb, in a warm worktree under the shared build lock (4 cores, 2 rustc jobs). (1) `cargo dev-test` at the merged head 308bef42d: 3,176 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored; librocksdb-sys not in its dependency graph, not compiled. (2) The release build of 308bef42d (reflow2 0.84.0) wrote proj:kept into a new folder's store (SSTs, MANIFEST, IDENTITY) and `--export` from a second process read it back; the on_disk program's 108 tests pass on the default build. (3) The refusal file: 4 of 4 failed on main e45225520 (--export printed the design; the server served the full surface; the --shared client started a daemon); 4 of 4 pass without the feature, and its default-build test passes with it. (4) With RocksDB: 1,176 tests in 173 programs on main → 1,180 on the branch, 0 lost, 4 new; at the merged head 1,191 (#755 added 11). Without RocksDB: 996 = 1,176 − 187 gated + 7 new; at the merged head 1,007, and the difference from the with-RocksDB list is exactly the 187 plus the one test that opens a store to show a default build does. The 187 are 108 tests in 19 files that are all disk (on_disk) and 79 marked one by one in 21 files; every one failed without the feature on the refusal or what it left, none for any other reason. (5) `cargo test -p reflow2-mcp` from `cargo clean -p reflow2-core -p reflow2-mcp`: before 173 test programs, 56.8 GB of executables, 57.1 GB added to target/debug/deps, 42.7 min; after 6 programs, 2.7 GB, 3.1 GB, 17.0 min; without RocksDB 5 programs, 0.9 GB, 1.2 GB, 10.6 min. The served tool list is byte-identical in both builds; all 198 toolsnaps match the default build. All MCP tests pass in both configurations at the merged head (1,189 passed with RocksDB; 1,005 without), core 2,129 passed with no features; clippy clean in all three configurations CI builds.
properties.name: Everyday builds run without RocksDB, installed builds keep it, and no test is lost to the four programs
